title: Two kinds of falling prices

controls.label: AD shift (billions at every price level)
SRAS shift (billions at every price level)

predict.q: The economy starts in long-run equilibrium: price level **110**, real output **2,000** (potential). Two different changes each cut the price level to **105**. Which one also raises unemployment?

options.fb: AD −125: price level 105, output 1,925, below potential, so unemployment rises.
A rise in SRAS moves the economy down along AD: prices fall and output rises to 2,050, so unemployment falls.

options.s: Both equally: falling prices always mean job losses
options.fb: Prices fall to 105 in both cases, but output goes opposite ways: 1,925 after the AD fall, 2,050 after the SRAS rise.

task: Move the AD slider left by **125**, reset, then move the SRAS slider right by **125**. Watch real output and unemployment.

target.do: Move AD to −125 (or SRAS to +125), then press Check. Use Reset to try the other.

takeaway: The same fall in prices can come with a slump (AD) or a boom (SRAS). The cause decides the cost.
